subject: P0: PioneerMed production — hotpath 5xx/429 surge
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@pioneermed.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Production: 5xx spike on /generate causing HL7 pipeline failures

Hi Rishi,

We just hit a major issue in production — starting ~08:40 PT we're seeing a sharp spike of 5xx responses and a cascade of 429s from your API on our HL7 ingestion path (/v1/generate). Our downstream workflow is retrying and now the queue is backing up. Error rates peaked at ~22% 5xx and intermittent 429 bursts over the last 45 minutes.

Impact: several hospitals are reporting delayed chart ingestion; one customer reported a full processing stall. This is customer-visible and we need immediate remediation and an ETA for stabilization.

What we need now:
- A short incident bridge (30m) with ops & eng (we can do PST-friendly times)
- Immediate mitigation recommendations (fallback model, rate-limits, temporary credits)
- Post-incident explanation and timeline for a durable fix

I've attached a small sample of request IDs and our token-usage CSV. Let me know the bridge link and who from Redwood will join.

Thanks,
Samantha
Head of Integrations, PioneerMed
Samantha.lee@pioneermed.com

Attachments: pioneer_sample_tokens.csv (sample), request-ids.txt

Can you confirm the window of impacted request IDs? Also please paste 3 example request-ids inline if you can, that'll speed up our logs lookup.

Subject: Re: Production: 5xx spike on /generate causing HL7 pipeline failures

On Sun, Apr 4, 2027 at 09:28 AM Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks for flagging, Samantha — sorry for the outage. We're standing up a short bridge now.

Quick incident summary from ops after initial triage:
- Symptom: brief but high-amplitude 5xx burst on the /v1/generate endpoint with concurrent 429s. Latency climbed from median 120ms to 1.2s before failures.
- Root cause hypthesis: Dedicated pool in us-west-2 experienced GPU exhaustion during a burst of large-batched requests originating from Pioneer's night queue. The autoscaler lagged because it hit a cloud quota and then failed several reconciliation cycles; new GPU nodes weren't provisioned fast enough.
- Amplifier: client's retry logic (aggressive immediate retries without backoff) created a retry storm which multiplied the load and pushed error rate higher.

Actions taken (done within the first 18 minutes):
1) Manual scale: increased Dedicated pool by 6 GPU units (manual add) and prioritized PioneerMed routing to those units.
2) Temporarily enabled per-client token bucket rate-limiter for PioneerMed to 120 req/min (configurable) to stop immediate retry amplification.
3) Routed multi-turn, non-critical requests to a smaller model variant (faster, lower memory) as an automatic fallback path.
4) Drained non-critical batch jobs and deferred lower-priority workloads to free capacity.

Next steps:
- Ben will open SUP-9981 (priority-high) for the autoscaler reconciliation failure and link cloud quota logs (he's added the initial notes).
- We'll perform a post-incident runbook review: add client-side recommended backoff guidance to our integration docs and a server-side circuit-breaker to avoid full-pool exhaustion.
- We can propose a short credit for customer impact; Rishi, can you coordinate commercial ask and SLA note?

Attachments: incident-graph.png (tokenized traffic x time), token-rate.csv (sample token usage window).

ETA for stabilization: services returned to normal within ~45 minutes after manual scale + rate-limiter. We've left the rate-limiter in place while we validate autoscaler fixes.

Marissa Cole
Head of Production Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Samantha Lee
